question: Is FV-versus-FIII source-classified initiation heterogeneity across projects still supported after allowing separate initiation baselines for every project × release year?
source: Pinned original six-project expert-corrected analysis/31_entry_state_score_transferability.py load; 575 fish; FIII/FV only; 2015 expert exclusions preserved.
design: Within each project-release-year stratum, fix FIII and FV counts and total classified initiators. Convolve year-wise Fisher noncentral hypergeometric combinatorial weights to a project-specific sufficient distribution for number of FV starts.
null: Common FV-vs-FIII odds ratio in all six projects, with unrestricted project-year baseline rates.
alternative: Project-specific FV-vs-FIII odds ratios, allowing separation and sparse cells.
exact_calibration: Condition additionally on sum of FV starts across six projects, eliminating common-odds nuisance exactly. Enumerate admissible six-project vectors and weight them by product of convolved combinatorial coefficients, using likelihood-ratio deviance.
predeclared_comparisons: leave-one-project-out exact p for all six omissions
unstratified six-project exact result as crosscheck
support/year-cell table to expose information loss
caveats: Both routes study source-algorithm initiation labels, not physiological migration initiation.
Year and project stratification remove different baseline rates, but cannot adjust animal-specific receiver detection or cue heterogeneity.
Only six projects; post-hoc heterogeneity discovery. Project-context mechanism is not identified.
If a release-year cell contains one stage or no outcome variation it contributes no stage contrast.
No retrospective changing of expert non-migrant corrections or source classification.
